The hidden cost of unguided rework

Blind rework is where boards go to die

Without vision and profile control, BGA rework is a gamble on the operator's hands — and every loss costs a board.

Alignment by eye fails

Fine-pitch BGAs cannot be aligned by eye. Off-center placement bridges balls or misses pads under the package.

One-sided heat warps

Heating a large board from one side lifts pads and warps the laminate. The board survives the first rework, barely.

Profiles are forgotten

Without stored profiles, every chip type is re-flowed by guesswork — hot spots burn, cold spots make fake joints.

Rework doubles the cost

A failed rework returns to the bench: the same labor, a second time, on a weaker board.

Quality is not auditable

Customers audit rework with documentation. Uncontrolled rework cannot show a curve, a profile or a pass record.

The bench never gets faster

Hand rework output is fixed by human hands, no matter how the order book grows.

Installation guide

From unpacking to first rework in five steps

Installation and operator training are included free with the SM-650.

01 · Bench & layout

Place the station on a stable workbench with clearance around the moving head. Provide fume extraction or ventilation above the working area.

02 · Utilities

Connect 220 VAC ±10% mains (single phase, ~5–8 kW depending on model). The vacuum pump and cooling fans are built in; no compressed air is required.

03 · Profiles & calibration

Set the reflow profile (rising and activity temperature segments) per BGA type, verify with the K-type thermocouple, and store the curve.

04 · Trial rework

Rework scrap boards first — check alignment, temperature balance (≤2 °C verified on the SM-650) and placement accuracy before production boards.

05 · Training & ramp

Free installation and operator training included; 24/7 worldwide support and 1-day spare-part lead time after handover.

Technical evaluation FAQ

Questions buyers ask before ordering

What makes the SM-650 a vision-class rework station?

The 27× color optical zoom vision system with dichroic and auto-focus functions overlays the IC image on the PCB image before placement, so the operator aligns BGA balls to pads on screen. Placement accuracy is verified within 0.05 mm.

What board and package sizes can it handle?

PCBs up to 550×500 mm (4 mm thick) and BGA packages up to 70×70 mm, with a maximum component weight of 80 g and minimum spacing of 0.30 mm.

How is the temperature controlled?

Three independent zones — top hot air (1200 W), lower hot air (800 W) and bottom IR (3600 W) — with 8-stage programmable temperature settings, real-time curve display and analysis. Temperature balance across the board is verified within 2 °C.

Can it store reflow profiles?

Yes. Profiles are stored on the embedded industrial PC, displayed on the touch screen and LCD monitor, and can be compared with historical saved curves — making the process repeatable and auditable.

What about large laptop motherboards?

The SM-650 includes special clamps for laptop motherboards plus adjustable anti-warpage support posts, so large boards heat evenly without sagging.

How do I get a quote and process recommendation?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your board samples or drawings, package sizes and rework volume. Configuration, quotation and profile strategy are provided within 24 hours.
